label: b3-check-R7
text:
These rules are for the agent's later session in /workspace. They do not apply to you: implement system enforcement for each rule with its enforcer, at its trigger, on its target.

Rule R7: 你所编写的代码文件内，所有类名的长度均需恰好为质数，不得有例外

- Route: Semgrep (Analysis › Code scans › Semgrep) · File write / edit (Agent action › File write / edit), timing: before · Class / type (Source code › Class / type)
- The check, by the enforcer: A pattern-based static analyzer. A rule is a code pattern that Semgrep matches against each file's syntax tree, for many languages (Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, HTML script blocks, Bash, …). Check: `semgrep scan --config <rules.yml> --error --metrics=off --quiet <file>` (exit 1 on a finding; `--json` for a report) Rules: `rules: [{id: <id>, languages: [<language>], severity: ERROR, message: "<what to change>", pattern: "<code pattern>"}]`; Semgrep matches syntax, it cannot compute values (a length, a count): let Semgrep find the code (`--json` gives each match's file, start and end lines), and compute the value from that in a check script (/opt/enforce-toolbox/skeletons/check.py) Start from the skeleton: /opt/enforce-toolbox/skeletons/semgrep_check.py (Semgrep finds the code; judge() decides, and computes what Semgrep cannot)
- Where it runs, by the trigger: the agent framework's hook (/opt/enforce-toolbox/mechanisms/framework-hooks.md) before its write tools (it sees the new content); file permissions (/opt/enforce-toolbox/mechanisms/file-permissions.md) (the write fails)
- What it reads, by the target: A class, a type, an interface or a struct. Where: in the source files (/opt/enforce-toolbox/skeletons/names_python.py, /opt/enforce-toolbox/skeletons/names_js.py)
- Tools: /opt/enforce/tool-installs/bin/semgrep: installed already; call each by this full path, since the agent's PATH does not have that folder
- Toolbox nodes: /opt/enforce-toolbox/enforcers/analysis/code-scans/semgrep.md, /opt/enforce-toolbox/triggers/agent-action/file-write-edit.md, /opt/enforce-toolbox/targets/source-code/class-type.md

Rule R2: 你所生成的所有代码文件都必须使用UTF-8进行编码

- Route: pre-commit (Gates › Git hooks › pre-commit) · File write / edit (Agent action › File write / edit), timing: before · Source file (Source code › Source file)
- The check, by the enforcer: A framework that runs the checks in a `.pre-commit-config.yaml` file when a commit is made. Check: a `.pre-commit-config.yaml` (local hooks: `repo: local`, `entry: <check>`) and `pre-commit install`; or `pre-commit run --files <file>` Start from the skeleton: /opt/enforce-toolbox/skeletons/pre_commit_check.sh (pre-commit runs a check on one file, outside a commit)
- Where it runs, by the trigger: the agent framework's hook (/opt/enforce-toolbox/mechanisms/framework-hooks.md) before its write tools (it sees the new content); file permissions (/opt/enforce-toolbox/mechanisms/file-permissions.md) (the write fails)
- What it reads, by the target: A source code file. Where: /workspace/<path>, on disk for every mechanism; the content of a write before it happens: only the framework's hook (/opt/enforce-toolbox/mechanisms/framework-hooks.md) before its write tool Which files: decide when the check runs, from the file in hand: the files the agent will create cannot be known before. Map its name, or its content, to a language with a complete list, such as Pygments (`get_lexer_for_filename`, `guess_lexer`) or GitHub Linguist's list of languages: programming and markup languages that hold code count (Python, JavaScript, HTML, CSS, shell, …); documents and data do not (Markdown, plain text, JSON, YAML, CSV), unless the rule names them. A rule about the file itself (its first lines, its name, its encoding) applies once per file, in that file's own comment syntax (in HTML, an HTML comment); a rule about the code in it (functions, names, statements) also reaches code embedded in another file, such as a `<script>` in HTML. A file whose kind is unknown is checked, not passed.
- Tools: /opt/enforce/tool-installs/bin/pre-commit: installed already; call each by this full path, since the agent's PATH does not have that folder
- Toolbox nodes: /opt/enforce-toolbox/enforcers/gates/git-hooks/pre-commit.md, /opt/enforce-toolbox/triggers/agent-action/file-write-edit.md, /opt/enforce-toolbox/targets/source-code/source-file.md

Rule R8: 必须保证输出的每一份代码文件，其文件名包含的字符个数严格等于奇数

- Route: Regex validator (Validation › Regex › Regex validator) · File write / edit (Agent action › File write / edit), timing: before · Source file (Source code › Source file)
- The check, by the enforcer: A regular expression that the checked text must match, or must not match. A match against the rule is a violation. What is read is part of the enforcer: a whole file, each line, only comments, a reply, the start or the end of a text. Check: a check script (/opt/enforce-toolbox/skeletons/check.py) with a regular expression; read what the rule is about (the whole text, each line, comments, the start or the end). The work for these rules comes as nodes, one at a time; when you reply to a node, the harness checks it. The nodes: check-R7, check-R2, check-R4, check-R8, binding-1.
Build exactly what each rule's route says. If a part of a route cannot work here, write why in /opt/enforce/deviations.json ({"R<n>": "<why>"}) and build the nearest thing that keeps the rest of the route.


Node check-R7 (1 of 5): write test cases and the check of R7. It runs the route's tool: /opt/enforce/tool-installs/bin/semgrep. The cases: at least two that break the rule, as files in /opt/enforce/fixtures/R7/flag, and at least two that follow it, in /opt/enforce/fixtures/R7/pass; each one file of what the check reads (A class, a type, an interface or a struct. Where: in the source files (/opt/enforce-toolbox/skeletons/names_python.py, /opt/enforce-toolbox/skeletons/names_js.py)). Cover every kind of input the rule reaches, as the agent may really write it: for files, several languages each in its own comment syntax (Python, JavaScript, HTML with a <script>, a shell script, …), and also files the rule does not cover, which must pass; for a reply, short and long replies, with lists and code blocks. The check: the executable /opt/enforce/checks/R7; `/opt/enforce/checks/R7 <file>` exits 0 when the file follows the rule, and otherwise exits 1 and prints each violation: R7, where (the file and line, or the part of the text), and what to change. The harness checks this when you reply.
